newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products rely on Asian demand for support.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products rely on Asian demand for support.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were supported only by Asian demand and were otherwise weak on Friday, traders said
Naphtha was easy in quiet trade. Talk remained mainly quotes related but outright prices were notionally assessed around $1 lower at $175/$178 a tonne cif, around $5-7 down on the week.
Gasoline held steady, supported by firmer NYMEX unleaded and light buying into Italy, the East Med and the Black Sea.
Premium unleaded cargoes for balance of April delivery talked around fob high quotes +$2 a tonne, equivalent to around $197 fob Med.
Asian interest underpinned gas oil, keeping prices strong. Some traders were thought keen on propelling levels higher for pricing purposes into India.
Italian 0.2 spec held onto high fob quotes +$4-5 while Russian cargoes were around high fob hiqh quotes +$5.
"These apply only to large cargoes that have the potential to be moved eastwards," said one trader.
Smaller cargoes attracted $2-3 lower while delivered parcels were around high cif quotes +$3.50. Diesel was $3 or so above the EN590 quote.
Fuel oil trade was limited. The German trader who bought 50kt of Italian end-April barrels reappeared in the market to snap up 30kt more from a trader to top-up a vessel that will head eastwards.
The price was reported to be $77 fob but believed to be higher. The arb window to Singapore or Fujairah was believed only just open and workable with cheap freight.
High sulphur cracked barrels were heard still abundant, undermining the supportive effect of the draw east-wards
